claim: A static network keeps reconnaissance valid and lets an attacker plan at its leisure.
quote: It is now clear that static systems present a substantial advantage to attackers. Attackers can observe the operation of key IT systems over long periods of time and plan attacks at their leisure, having mapped out an inventory of assets, vulnerabilities, and exploits.
issue: 'Keeps reconnaissance valid' is the sense of 'having mapped out an inventory' on a system that stays static; 'systems' (addresses, names, software stacks, networks) covers 'network'. Note: the text cache appends a second document (ghosh2009nitrd.md, a Moving Target Defense section with the wording 'look the same for a long time'); quoted the cited Co-Chairs' Report PDF instead.

claim: MTD aims to shift the advantage of time from the attacker to the defender.
quote: For instance, by the time an adversary discovers a vulnerability in a service, the service will have changed its attack surface area so that an-other exploit against that vulnerability will be ineffective.
issue: Ghosh says static systems advantage attackers who observe over long periods (p. 31) and that MTD makes discovered vulnerabilities go stale; it never frames MTD as giving the advantage to the defender, nor as an advantage 'of time'. The 'shift' framing must rest on co-cite zhuang2012 (not checked here).
fix_text: Keep if zhuang2012 carries the 'advantage shifts to the defender' wording; otherwise tighten to 'MTD aims to remove the advantage a static network gives the attacker'.
